ideas.hypothesis: Station areas that unbundle and price residential parking experience slower rent escalation and less income turnover than station areas with bundled free parking, because unbundling lowers housing costs for car-free households.

sources.role: finding: TOD parking supply and pricing rarely support transit goals
mechanism: TOD can disrupt low-income neighborhoods
mechanism: less parking lowers development cost

ideas.test: Compare California rail station areas with and without unbundled parking requirements using ACS tract data (median rent, income change) 2000-2019 in a difference-in-differences design.
ideas.disconfirming: Rent growth and income turnover are equal or higher where parking is priced.

ideas.hypothesis: Providing car sharing in lieu of parking in TOD housing allows more low-income households to remain near stations, reducing displacement relative to parking-heavy TOD.

sources.role: mechanism: carsharing substitutes for parking in small TOD
concept: car sharing for car-free city

ideas.test: Survey residents of TOD buildings with and without on-site car share in Bay Area; compare share of low-income tenants retained over 5 years using lease records.
ideas.disconfirming: Tenant retention of low-income households is no higher in car-share buildings.

ideas.hypothesis: The effective walking distance to rail stations shrinks in winter where sidewalk snow clearance is poor, so station catchments in cold cities are overestimated by fixed-radius TOD definitions.

sources.role: concept: TOD defined by walking distance

ideas.test: Use farecard tap-ins and home-location surveys in Minneapolis light rail station areas; compare distance-decay curves between winter months with differing municipal sidewalk clearing policies.
ideas.disconfirming: Distance-decay is the same in winter and summer regardless of clearance policy.

ideas.hypothesis: Bus shelter provision near TOD is lower in low-income tracts, and adding shelters raises ridership more among low-income riders than other riders.
ideas.test: Inventory shelters at stops in Chicago region; regress shelter presence on tract income; before-after ridership comparison at stops receiving new shelters.
ideas.disconfirming: Shelter distribution is income-neutral and new shelters have no differential ridership effect.

ideas.hypothesis: Car-sharing membership around stations increases with intersection density because fine-grained street grids support car-free living with occasional car access.

sources.role: finding: built environment affects vehicle ownership

ideas.test: Cross-sectional regression of car-share members per household on intersection density in half-mile station areas across several US metros, controlling for income and transit frequency.
ideas.disconfirming: No association once density and income are controlled.

ideas.hypothesis: Combined housing-plus-transportation cost burdens in TOD are more sensitive to fare policy than to rent levels for low-income households, so fare discounts improve TOD affordability more than equal-cost rent subsidies.
ideas.test: Simulate H+T costs for low-income households in station areas using ACS and travel survey data under alternative fare discount and rent subsidy scenarios of equal cost.
ideas.disconfirming: Rent subsidies reduce H+T burden as much or more than fare discounts.

ideas.hypothesis: Form-based or TOD overlay zoning codes produce higher intersection density in new station-area development than conventional use-based codes.
ideas.test: Compare street network changes 2005-2019 within 800 m of Phoenix light rail stations under overlay vs conventional zoning using GIS street data.
ideas.disconfirming: Intersection density growth does not differ by zoning type.

ideas.hypothesis: Station areas served by dedicated TOD acquisition funds with CDFI lending experience less low-income displacement than comparable station areas without such funds.

sources.role: finding: Denver TOD fund preserves affordability

ideas.test: Match Denver station areas with TOD fund acquisitions to similar areas without; compare change in low-income household share from ACS.
ideas.disconfirming: No difference in low-income household change.

ideas.hypothesis: Ridership forecasts made with structured stakeholder workshops (serious gaming) have smaller forecast errors than forecasts made by models alone, because local actors anticipate development timing.

sources.role: method: serious game for TOD stakeholders
finding: standard trip rates misestimate TOD travel

ideas.test: Compare forecast vs actual ridership for station projects with and without documented stakeholder-based scenario exercises in the Netherlands.
ideas.disconfirming: Forecast errors are no smaller with stakeholder engagement.

ideas.hypothesis: Land use scenario models that include rent-dependent household relocation predict post-TOD income change better than models with fixed populations.
ideas.test: Backcast income change around a past light rail opening (e.g., Minneapolis Hiawatha) with two model versions and compare to observed ACS data.
ideas.disconfirming: The relocation-aware model predicts no better.

ideas.hypothesis: Relocating government offices to suburban transit centers improves job access for low-income workers in outer suburbs more than residential TOD does.
ideas.test: Accessibility analysis using GTFS and census employment data for Perth before and after office decentralisation, broken down by income quintile.
ideas.disconfirming: Accessibility gains are concentrated among high-income workers.

ideas.hypothesis: Higher density of public seating and street furniture in station plazas raises resident-reported sense of place and dwell time, distinguishing TOD from transit-adjacent development.
ideas.test: Audit furniture at 20 station plazas and survey users on place attachment; regress scores on furniture density.
ideas.disconfirming: No association between furniture and sense of place.

ideas.hypothesis: Perceived safety at stations extends the walking distance people accept to reach transit, especially for women and night trips.
ideas.test: Intercept survey at stations recording access distance and perceived safety; estimate distance-decay by safety score.
ideas.disconfirming: Accepted walking distance is independent of perceived safety.

ideas.hypothesis: Providing free transit passes to TOD residents allows parking ratios to be cut without increasing on-street spillover.

sources.role: finding: lower auto trips in TOD

ideas.test: Compare parking occupancy and resident car ownership at California TOD projects with and without bundled passes.
ideas.disconfirming: Pass programs show no difference in parking occupancy.

ideas.hypothesis: Car-share availability lowers TOD vehicle trip generation below ITE rates by an amount beyond that explained by transit proximity alone.

sources.role: finding: ITE rates overestimate TOD trips

ideas.test: Driveway counts at TOD housing with and without on-site car share, matched on station distance.
ideas.disconfirming: Trip rates are equal.

ideas.hypothesis: In small towns with bus transit, reducing downtown parking minimums near stops increases infill development without reducing retail sales.

sources.role: setting: transit-oriented design in small cities
mechanism: less parking supports small-scale TOD

ideas.test: Compare permits and sales tax trends in small towns that reformed parking minimums with matched towns that did not.
ideas.disconfirming: Infill does not rise or sales fall.

ideas.hypothesis: BRT openings produce smaller residential displacement effects than rail openings with similar ridership because land value capitalization is weaker.
ideas.test: Event-study of tract income composition around BRT vs light rail openings in US metros.
ideas.disconfirming: Displacement indicators are similar or larger for BRT.

ideas.hypothesis: Station areas with active community organizations are more likely to adopt reduced parking requirements when organizations frame parking as an affordability issue.

sources.role: finding: parking policy shapes TOD economics

ideas.test: Document parking reforms and community organization involvement in 30 station-area plans; logistic regression.
ideas.disconfirming: Organization presence does not predict parking reform.

ideas.hypothesis: Mixed-use station neighborhoods have lower per-capita traffic emissions but higher local pollutant exposure near busy stations, an exposure trade-off.

sources.role: claim: TOD expected to improve air quality

ideas.test: Low-cost sensor monitoring in mixed-use vs single-use station areas paired with VMT estimates.
ideas.disconfirming: Both emissions and exposure are lower in mixed-use areas.

ideas.hypothesis: Projects with higher federal funding shares are followed by declines in racial and income diversity in station areas unless affordability requirements are attached.
ideas.test: Merge New Starts project funding with tract diversity indices pre/post opening.
ideas.disconfirming: Funding share is unrelated to diversity change.

ideas.hypothesis: Targeted transit marketing to new TOD residents raises transit use most among households that recently moved and have fewer cars.

sources.role: question: best ways to promote TOD ridership
measure: household characteristics and mode share

ideas.test: Randomized marketing outreach to new TOD residents; measure transit trips via farecards by household type.
ideas.disconfirming: No heterogeneous effect by household characteristics.

ideas.hypothesis: Converting park-and-ride lots to joint development accelerates station-area gentrification more than greenfield TOD.

sources.role: finding: replacement parking in joint development

ideas.test: Compare tract change around converted lots vs retained lots in Bay Area and Atlanta.
ideas.disconfirming: No difference in income or rent change.

ideas.hypothesis: Bike lane connectivity to stations reduces vehicle trip generation at TOD housing beyond walking-catchment effects.

sources.role: finding: TOD trip rates below ITE

ideas.test: Driveway counts at TOD sites regressed on bike network connectivity metrics.
ideas.disconfirming: Bike connectivity unrelated to trip rates.

ideas.hypothesis: Joint-development PPPs at stations are followed by service frequency increases because agencies gain revenue and ridership.
ideas.test: Panel of stations with GTFS frequency before/after PPP agreements versus non-PPP stations.
ideas.disconfirming: Frequency unchanged.

ideas.hypothesis: Traffic calming within station areas increases station boardings by improving pedestrian access.

sources.role: measure: transit use at Portland TODs

ideas.test: Before-after boardings at Portland stations with new traffic calming vs controls.
ideas.disconfirming: No boarding change.

ideas.hypothesis: Priced parking at TOD retail does not reduce retail sales when transit frequency is high.
ideas.test: Compare sales per square foot at TOD retail centers with paid vs free parking, stratified by frequency.
ideas.disconfirming: Sales are lower with paid parking even at high frequency.

ideas.hypothesis: Regions with metropolitan governments enforcing regional housing targets show less station-area displacement.
ideas.test: Compare displacement indicators across metros with stronger vs weaker regional governance.
ideas.disconfirming: No governance difference.

ideas.hypothesis: Frequency at the nearest station predicts lower household car ownership more strongly than station distance.

sources.role: finding: vehicle ownership differs across BART stations
method: regression of commuting on urban form

ideas.test: Household travel survey with GTFS frequency and distance; ordered logit of vehicles owned.
ideas.disconfirming: Frequency is insignificant once distance included.

ideas.hypothesis: Bundled parking costs raise TOD rents disproportionately for low-income transit riders who do not own cars.
ideas.test: Estimate parking cost share of rent and car ownership by income in TOD buildings using surveys.
ideas.disconfirming: Parking cost burden is not higher for low-income riders.

ideas.hypothesis: Neighborhoods around SkyTrain stations with sustained densification increased ethnic and income diversity more than non-station neighborhoods.
ideas.test: Canadian census tract diversity indices 1986-2016 comparing station vs matched non-station areas.
ideas.disconfirming: Diversity change is no greater near stations.
